headline: Public hearings on utility conduits, zoning changes, and a 27 Chandler St. housing tax exemption.
summary: The meeting also covers city grants and budget transfers, pay changes for many job groups, and about 54 resident petitions on traffic and street issues. A petition asks for an ordinance allowing licensed cannabis social consumption establishments.
items: Public hearing on a Charter Communications conduit at 135 Kenberma Rd.
Public hearing on National Grid conduits at Main St. and Newbury St.
Request to add 416 Belmont St. and nearby lots to the Commercial Corridor Overlay district, sent to Planning Board
About 54 petitions on streets, signs, speed humps, and parking, sent to committees
Request for Community Clothing Closets, sent to Public Health and Human Services Committee
Set a November 17, 2026 hearing on two National Grid conduits at 116 and 124 Rodney St.
Request for an ordinance allowing licensed cannabis social consumption establishments
Board and commission appointments and reappointments, including Affordable Housing Trust Fund and Citizens Advisory Council
Tax Increment Exemption Agreement and housing project resolution for 27 Chandler St. and 53 Irving St.
FY27 tax classification options, budget adjustments, and Elderly Exemption Program order
Department reports on Veterans Services relocation, tree inspections, rodeo draft ordinance, and August 2026 finances
Grants and donations: $350,000 National Endowment for the Humanities, $192,247.25 State 911, $200,000 DESE, $23,800 United Way, $500 donation
Budget transfers and payments for prior-year invoices
Rezoning of 13 properties near Grove and Brookfield streets from manufacturing to business
Rezoning of three Milton St. properties to residential
Zoning change for 455 Grove St.
Belmont and Plantation streets corridor zoning amendment
Extending business and overlay zoning to properties on Charlton, Hermon, and Beacon streets
Report on converting part of Marmion Ave. from private to public street, sent to Public Works
Sewer extensions on Arlington St. and Henchman St.
Public health reports on roaming cats, miniature alcohol bottles, and winter shelters, mostly placed on file
10 traffic and parking reports recommended for adoption, and 18 placed on file
Ordinance to create a tow zone on portions of Albany St. and Fantasia Dr.
Salary ordinance changes for 25 job groups and members of Local 495, NAGE
Update on U.S. Department of Justice report on the Worcester Police Department, held under privilege
Five older tabled items, including rent control and an Office of Housing Stability
Five orders from the October 20 meeting: four adopted, one held under privilege
13 committee requests to city departments on parking, crosswalks, and road work
19 orders from councilors, including student loan repayment help and an emergency preparedness plan
Resolution recognizing Brig. Gen. Richard P. Cipro
Four Library Board of Directors vacancies filled
Worcester Public Schools easement request to National Grid on Oberlin St. and Woodland St.
Worcester Public Schools lease of ten special education buses for five years
location: Esther Howland (South) Chamber, City Hall, 455 Main Street, Worcester, Massachusetts

Important Notice: Residents are advised of an ongoing scam involving the 
impersonation of city officials and departments. Scammers are fraudulently requesting 
payments be made for planning and zoning permits, as well as City Council petitions . 
All official emails regarding your petition will come exclusively from an 
@worcesterma.gov email address (such as clerk @worcesterma.gov), or via physical 
mail on the City of Worcester’s official letterhead. Any legitimate hearing letter will 
always include your specific application details, along with the scheduled hearing date , 
time, and location. The City of Worcester will never request payments via wire transfer.
